messages:
alex: Heads-up — incoming from Acme support. They say embeddings billing (invoice 2025-03-01) is ~3x what the dashboard shows. Attached example: a single batched request of 10 short strings was billed as 12 units on the invoice. request_id=req_acme_001

sara: Thanks, I'll triage. Can you paste the exact API payload and the invoice line item IDs? Also need customer's workspace_id.

alex: Payload snippet they pasted:```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-1536",
  "inputs": ["short str 1", "short str 2", "... x10 ..."]
}
```They say dashboard (console->Embeddings->Usage) shows 10 inputs for that time window. invoice line: INV-2025-03-01-ACME-L1, billing_units=12. workspace_id=ws_acme_42

miguel: I'm looking at meter logs for model=redwood-embed-1536 around ts 1750001200-1750001300. Can you grab the service request_id the customer provided? We need the server-side request_id (X-Request-ID) not the client's.

alex: Customer gave client Request-Id req_acme_001 and says server returned x-request-id: srv-7f9a2. I pulled logs and see a batch worker that split the request into two sub-batches: sizes 6 and 4. Server meters incremented counters: embedding_inputs=10 but billing_units=12.

john: Billing here. Two possible explanations we've seen: 1) per-input rounding rules (we bill by embedding token units, rounded up to nearest N), 2) an earlier billing-only path double-counted inputs when a fallback quantized model was used. Any model fallback in logs?

miguel: Good call. Logs show a fallback to "redwood-embed-1536-quant" for sub-batch size 6 due to temp capacity. The runtime emits meter events: `meter.event(type=embedding_request, inputs=6, tokens=4800)` and `meter.event(type=embedding_request, inputs=4, tokens=320)`. But I also see a downstream billing adapter receiving two events with slightly different semantics: one carries `raw_inputs=6`, the other `accounting_units= (tokens/1024 rounded up)`. There was a mismatch in our translator v1.9 that counted `accounting_units` per-sub-batch and then again per-input in the same request for quantized fallbacks.

eng-ml-bot: (automated) Known issue #ENG-ML-1483: meter->billing translator double-counts when fallback_to_quantized=true AND batch_splitting=true. Patch staged.

sara: OK — customer impact: incorrect extra charges. What's the scope? Any other customers affected?

miguel: Quick scan of the last 24h shows ~120 requests across ~15 customers hit the exact translation path. Most are small, but the aggregated delta is ~0.6% of daily embeddings usage. We'll need to reconcile invoices for the affected customers.

john: I'll prepare credits for affected invoices. Need CSV with: workspace_id, invoice_id, billed_units, dashboard_units, delta_units, request_ids. Can you export that?

miguel: On it. Also adding a check in the telemetry to compare `dashboard_inputs` vs `billing_units` per-request and flag >5% mismatches.

alex: For Acme specifically — they want repro steps so they can verify once we fix. Miguel, can you write minimal repro and confirm which SDK versions triggered the bug?

miguel: Repro steps: 1) Use model `redwood-embed-1536` with `batch_size=10` and enable `allow_quant_fallback=true`. 2) Send single request with 10 short inputs. 3) Force a quant fallback by temporarily setting capacity threshold low (or mock a 503 on main kernel). 4) Observe meter entries in logs and check billing adapter events. Example curl:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1536","inputs":["a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h","i","j"],"allow_quant_fallback":true,"batching":true}'
```Run and check server log lines: `meter: inputs=10 tokens_est=800`, `billing: accounting_units=12`

alex: Perfect. Sara, can you ask Acme to run that curl from their environment (or we can run it in a repro account) and paste the server x-request-id?

sara: Reached out, they replied with srv-7f9a2 (same as earlier). I attached the full server logs from that timestamp.

miguel: I reproduced locally by flipping the translator to v1.9 and forcing fallback. Confirmed double-count: billing_adapter was incremented twice for the 6-item sub-batch (once for raw count, once for accounting_units). Root cause: translator merges `raw_count` and `accounting_units` events when quant fallback tag present, but then billing adapter applied both fields.

john: Scope for credits: I'll compute per-workspace delta and propose full refund for the extra units. For Acme INV-2025-03-01-ACME-L1, delta_units=2 -> will issue credit line and notify them.

miguel: Patch status: branch fix/ENG-ML-1483 created. Behavioral fix: translator now emits a single canonical `billing_units` field and billing adapter ignores `raw_count` when `billing_units` present. Tests added for batch-splitting + fallback. Deploy scheduled in 30m to canary, 2h to prod if canary looks good.

ops-bot: (deploy) Rolling canary deploy of service redwood-meters v2025.04.02-canary to zone us-west-2 -> started.

alex: I'll reply to Acme: apology + short summary + promise of credit and ETA for fix. Sara, please include request_id and invoice id in the note.

sara: Message sent to Acme: "Thanks — we found a bug causing duplicate billing when quantized fallbacks + batch splitting occur. We're patching now and will credit the extra units on INV-2025-03-01-ACME-L1. ETA for fix: 2h. Customer replied :thumbsup:."

miguel: Canary looks clean. No extra meter deltas. Promoting to prod in 2h.

john: Credits queued. I'll follow up in billing queue once deploy is prod.

alex: Closing loop: add postmortem note in #postmortems once billing actions finish. Good triage — nice work. :tada:
